sections.label: Questions to the Minister
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister two questions and seeks clarification on whether the Motion has two points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But before I deliver my speech, Speaker, may I ask the Minister two questions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, Minister, can I clarify, your Motion basically has two points.

sections.label: HDB resale price index
sections.summary: Since 1990 the HDB resale price index rose seven times while median monthly household income rose only four times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Since 1990, the HDB resale price index has increased by seven times as a result of the Asset Enhancement policies of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But the median monthly household income has only increased four times.

sections.label: CPF savings for housing loans
sections.summary: January Government data shows the bottom 40% income bracket uses a median over 70% of monthly CPF contributions for housing loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: However, this comes at the cost of depleting their CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: This is backed by the latest data released by the Government in January in response to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's question, which shows for those at the bottom 40% income bracket, the median percentage of monthly CPF contributions used to service housing loans is more than 70%.

sections.label: Tengah BTO flat CPF cost
sections.summary: A new 4-room BTO flat at Tengah initially costing $350,000 will cost the buyer $592,000 in CPF savings after 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: A new 4-room BTO flat at Tengah, which initially cost $350,000, will actually cost the buyer $592,000 in CPF savings after 25 years of principal repayment and financing costs.

sections.label: HDB prices and land cost
sections.summary: High HDB prices from rising land cost deplete CPF savings while HDB pays $3 billion to $4 billion in land cost into past reserves yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Currently, high HDB prices caused by rising land cost are raiding the CPF savings of Singaporeans, while HDB pays $3 billion to $4 billion in land cost into the past reserves each year.

sections.label: Young couples waiting for BTO flats
sections.summary: The problem has worsened and close to 100,000 young couples are waiting for BTO flats, some more than five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The problem has worsened since then, and currently, close to 100,000 young couples are waiting for their BTO flats, some more than five years already.

sections.label: Tengah BTO flat payment
sections.summary: A Singaporean buyer paid about $140,000 of a $350,000 Tengah BTO flat, with the $210,000 land cost balance paid later into the past reserve after MOP sale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: In the same example of the Tengah BTO flat, whereas the full price is $350,000, the Singaporean buyer only paid the user price of about $140,000 at the time of the purchase under the Affordable Homes Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The balance of $210,000 in land cost will be paid later into the past reserve, when the flat is sold after the MOP.

sections.label: Millennial Apartments leases
sections.summary: The Millennial Apartments will be smaller, quality flats on affordable two-to-five-year leases for younger families or groups of singles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The Millennial Apartments will be smaller and quality flats on affordable leases of two to five years for younger families or groups of singles.

sections.label: Two schemes future benefits
sections.summary: The two schemes would make owner-occupied public housing affordable by waiving land cost, allow retirement without downgrading, offer more choices, and keep the resale market buoyant but less speculative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: With the two schemes, Singaporeans can look forward to a better future where: one, owner-occupied public housing is truly affordable as land cost is waived; two, they can have enough to retire without having to downgrade or sell back their lease to the Government; three, they have more choices to choose what best suits their life plans and aspiration, to buy or to rent, to be an HDB occupier or an investor and others; four, the resale market remains buoyant although less speculative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: It is important to reiterate that the two schemes will not raid the reserves, no matter what the Government may say.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We only need the Government to make up its mind and we can execute the reset as swiftly as we had tackled the COVID-19 pandemic.
